notes: `חֹזֵה הַמֶּלֶךְ` is read by rule 29's possessive paragraph: the phrase's *the* determines the possessor, so it goes to the article on `מֶלֶךְ` and not to the construct.
`דִבְרֵי הָאֱלֹהִים` is the fronting case of rule 29, the ASV rendering the rectum anarthrously (*of God*), so the article's *the* stands before *words* and the construct keeps only its own word.
`הָרִים` → *lift up* keeps its particle with the verb: the elevation `רוּם` writes is written in the clause, so rule 44's surplus-particle sentence does not reach it.
The article of the second `הָאֱלֹהִים` is `unrepresented`, the ASV writing *God* with no determiner (rule 29).
